Assignment: dialect `postgres`. The notes below were written for a bigger task; use only their engine, version and doc-source information.

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. PL/pgSQL bodies are dollar-quoted strings the server parses later, so probe CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE forms (LANGUAGE, RETURNS TABLE/SETOF, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER, SET, PARALLEL, SQL-standard BEGIN ATOMIC bodies, RETURN expr) rather than PL/pgSQL statements. Query syntax includes DISTINCT ON, LATERAL, TABLESAMPLE, ROWS FROM, WITH ORDINALITY, GROUPING SETS/CUBE/ROLLUP, FILTER, WINDOW clause and frame exclusion, FOR UPDATE/SHARE/NO KEY UPDATE/KEY SHARE with NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED, FETCH ... WITH TIES, recursive CTE SEARCH/CYCLE, MATERIALIZED CTEs, data-modifying CTEs, INSERT ON CONFLICT, RETURNING, MERGE (incl. RETURNING and WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE), JSON_TABLE, array/composite/range literals. Engine: PostgreSQL 17. Doc entry points: SQL commands https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-commands.html ; SELECT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html ; lexical structure https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-syntax-lexical.html ; value expressions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-expressions.html ; functions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions.html ; data types https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype.html . pglast (the real PostgreSQL parser) is a reliable reference: a probe pglast rejects is almost certainly invalid SQL.

Scope: "rest": every statement in the vendor's statement index that isn't in the brief's core list. No expressions section. That's about 150 of the 183 SQL commands (aggregates, casts, collations, domains, event triggers, extensions, FDW objects, operators, policies, publications, roles, rules, sequences, statistics, subscriptions, tablespaces, text search, triggers, types, user mappings; ANALYZE, CALL, CHECKPOINT, CLUSTER, COMMENT, COPY, cursors, DISCARD, DO, LISTEN/NOTIFY, LOCK, PREPARE/EXECUTE, REINDEX, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, SET/RESET/SHOW, VACUUM, ...). COPY is high tier and needs depth (FROM/TO, STDIN/STDOUT/PROGRAM, query source, WITH options, legacy options). Engine: PostgreSQL 17. Doc entry points: SQL commands https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-commands.html ; SELECT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html ; lexical structure https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-syntax-lexical.html ; value expressions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-expressions.html ; functions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions.html ; data types https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype.html . pglast (the real PostgreSQL parser) is a reliable reference: a probe pglast rejects is almost certainly invalid SQL.
